ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. If $\angle ADB=30^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle AOB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since ABCD is a rectangle,\\
it follows that $\angle$DAB = 90$^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle$ADB = 30$^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle$ABD = 90$^\circ - \angle$ADB = 60$^\circ$.\\
Since OA = OB,\\
it follows that $\triangle$ABO is an equilateral triangle,\\
therefore, $\angle$AOB = \boxed{60^\circ}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a quadrilateral ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right, and the whole is a rectangle; the two diagonals AC and BD intersect at the interior point O, and O is located on diagonal BD. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a rectangle, ∠DAB=90°. It is known that ∠ADB=30°; in the right triangle ABD, ∠ABD=90°-30°=60°. Since O is on BD, ray BO and BD are on the same straight line, therefore ∠ABO=∠ABD=60°. The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so AO=BO. Thus triangle AOB is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠BAO and ∠ABO are equal; since ∠ABO=60°, then ∠BAO=60°, so ∠AOB=180°-60°-60°=60°.
